summary: France faces a day of nationwide protests Saturday, including demonstrations inspired by the Yellow Vests, a sometimes radical grassroots movement that emerged in 2018 to fight rising living costs.

title: Rockstar Rebuilt Itself to Make GTA VI
summary: Bloomberg News video game reporter Jason Schreier tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Rockstar Games nearly doubled its workforce and overhauled its production culture while building the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI. Speaking with hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo, Schreier explains Rockstar’s efforts to curb excessive overtime, the extraordinary commercial expectations for the game and why the company believes its next major release could take less time to develop. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Puts New Russia Sanctions on Hold
summary: Bloomberg News Russia economy and government editor Anthony Halpin and White House correspondent Jeff Mason tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s waiver of new Russia sanctions could offer Moscow economic and diplomatic opportunities while adding pressure on Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protest Leader Released After Voter-List Row
summary: The founder of India’s “Cockroach” protest movement was released on Saturday after being taken into police custody, his lawyer said, as a widening fight over the country’s voter rolls keeps New Delhi on edge.

title: Stellantis Plans to Hire Hundreds More Engineers in Europe, US
summary: Stellantis NV Chief Engineering and Technology Officer Ned Curic plans to continue hiring more engineers as the automaker rolls out dozens of new models as part of its turnaround plan.

title: Oil Trader Yaoyao Liu Who Made Billions for Vitol Is Leaving
summary: Yaoyao Liu, whose trading in oil derivatives made billions of dollars for Vitol Group over a career marked by dramatic highs and lows, is leaving the commodities trading giant.

title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
summary: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville’s time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment”a mainstream term. title: China Warns Corrupt Officials Can’t Expect a Safe Landing
summary: China’s top anti-graft authorities warned that officials who engage in corruption cannot expect a “safe landing,” regardless of their rank, past contributions or whether they’ve retired, according to a commentary from the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Commission of Supervision.

title: Japan’s Takaichi to Attend APEC in China if Parliament Allows
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she plans to attend the APEC leaders summit hosted by China if parliament permits, confirming her willingness to visit amid a deep freeze of ties between the two Asian economies.

title: Fairfax’s Watsa Bets On IDBI Payoff As India Booms, Report Says
summary: Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa is betting that his Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.’s acquisition of IDBI Bank Ltd. will pay off given India’s growth prospects, the Economic Times reported.

title: India Halts Sugar Diversion to Ethanol After El Nino Hurts Crops
summary: India has ordered state-owned fuel retailers to stop procuring ethanol made from sugar and key sugarcane-based feedstocks in move that may help keep a lid on prices of the sweetener.

title: China Encourages Cinemas to Add Sports Events and Lottery Sales
summary: China is encouraging cinemas to screen major sporting events, host sports activities and sell sports lottery tickets as part of a drive to link moviegoing with sports consumption, according to a notice from the National Film Administration and General Administration of Sport.

title: Indonesia Unveils $117 Million in Fines After MSCI Warning
summary: Indonesia announced about $117 million in fines tied to manipulative market practices involving three companies, hours after global index provider MSCI Inc. said it was weighing a downgrade of the country’s stock market over investability concerns.

title: Vietnam Prime Minister Targets 2027 GDP Growth of at Least 10%
summary: Vietnam’s Prime Minister Le Minh Hung projected gross domestic product will expand at least 10% next year as he outlined the nation’s economic targets in a speech to parliament.

title: Jio’s $3.2 Billion IPO Tests Ambani Appeal With India’s Gen Z
summary: For generations of Indians, Reliance Industries Ltd. was their introduction to the stock market. Founder Dhirubhai Ambani drew middle-income savers into shares, building a following that endured for decades.

title: US Gives Green Light for New Routes from Mexico City Airports
summary: The US will allow Mexican airlines to offer new flights into the country from Mexico City’s two biggest airports, lifting restrictions that had blocked additional routes.

title: Chinese Stocks Turn Biggest Losers as Global AI Trade Stumbles
summary: Chinese firms have emerged as the biggest losers of the faltering global AI trade, a setback for Beijing’s efforts to use stock markets to supercharge its ambition of technological supremacy.

title: Graza CEO on Market Expansion, Consumer Outlook
summary: Andrew Benin, CEO of Graza, said the company’s appeal starts with the quality of its olive oil, while its squeezable bottle helped make the product approachable and popular. Benin emphasized sourcing transparency: bottles identify the oil’s origin, varietal, harvest season, bottling date and best-by date, while the brand aims to deliver a consistent peppery, flavor-forward profile despite agricultural variability. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: TGI Fridays CEO on Company Turnaround, Expansion Plans
summary: Ray Blanchette, CEO of TGI Fridays, says the restaurant aims to stand out in casual dining through value, quality food and attentive service. He identifies food, service and atmosphere as the priorities for attracting customers, with a renewed focus on scratch cooking and bringing energy back to the business. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chip Stocks Post Longest Losing Streak Since 2008: Markets Wrap
summary: Another burst of selling in technology shares drove the Nasdaq 100 to its worst week since the April 2025 tariff turmoil as investors questioned the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade.

title: Euro Snaps Five-Week Losing Streak With Warsh Remarks
summary: The euro halted a five-week slide against the dollar after comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh were interpreted as supporting the case for the US central bank to keep interest rates on hold this month.
